Definition: from G4710; to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest:--do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.
BiblicalUsage: To be diligent is to make haste with care. Study to shew thyself approved unto God, endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace, and let us labour therefore to enter into that rest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe diligence is the shape of faithfulness: study the word, keep the peace, and labour to enter the rest.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
